data.name: Jageshwar
data.gender_notes: Jageshwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jage means 'conqueror' and Ishwar means 'god'. So, Jageshwar is the 'God who conquers'. This name is associated with Lord Shiva, who is often depicted as the lord of the jungle or the destroyer of evil. The name Jageshwar carries the meaning “Lord of the Jungle” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jageshwar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the jungle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, courage, and protection against adversities.
data.etymology: Jageshwar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Jungle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jageshwar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ganesha is widely recognized and celebrated not just in India but also around the world. It symbolizes the power of wisdom and the removal of obstacles. The elephant-headed god is a revered symbol of Hindu culture and mythology.
data.spiritual_significance: According to Hindu scriptures, Lord Ganesha is the god of wisdom and the remover of obstacles. He is considered the deity of knowledge and the patron of learning. His statue is often installed at the entrance of temples and homes for blessings and protection.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jageshwar: Lord of Conquering Grace. This name symbolizes the supreme power and grace of Shiva, who conquers the ego and desires of the individual, leading to spiritual enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Jageshwar is a revered Hindu pilgrimage site located in the Himalayan region of Uttarakhand, India. It is believed that the Lord Shiva came to this place in the form of Jageshwar, in order to attack the demon Bhagirathi who was troubling the gods.

Another belief is that Jageshwar was the capital of the Katyuri dynasty, a powerful ruling house in medieval India. The Katyuris were known to be great patrons of art and architecture, and the temple complex at Jageshwar, with its 124 temples, is a testament to their cultural legacy.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Jageshwar' is popularly known for its significance in Hindu mythology and is a significant tourist destination. It is a popular pilgrimage site for Hindus, with many temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. The natural beauty of Jageshwar has led to its promotion as an eco-tourism destination. It can be easily located on Google Maps for travel planning and is frequently discussed on social media and travel websites.
